statement: For a valid phrase p, let firstWord(p) be p[0..f], where f = min{ g | 0<=g<len(p) and p[g]=32 } if this set is nonempty, otherwise f=len(p). Let lastWord(p) be p[l..len(p)], where l=0 if p has no space, otherwise l=1+max{ g | 0<=g<len(p) and p[g]=32 }. For a valid phrase q, let suffixAfterFirstWord(q) be q[f..len(q)] where f is as for firstWord(q). For valid phrases p,q, let merge(p,q) be the concatenation of p and suffixAfterFirstWord(q). The function returns a result r (so it does not fail) and, with this notation, for every byte array s, s occurs in r (meaning there exists k with 0<=k<len(r) and r[k]=s) if and only if there exist indices i,j with 0<=i<len(phrases), 0<=j<len(phrases), i != j, lastWord(phrases[i])=firstWord(phrases[j]), and s=merge(phrases[i],phrases[j]); moreover, for every k with 0<=k<len(r)-1, r[k] < r[k+1] in standard lexicographic order on byte arrays (a proper prefix is smaller than the longer array; otherwise the first differing byte decides by its unsigned value).
preconditions: len(phrases) is between 1 and 100 inclusive. For every i with 0 <= i < len(phrases), p = phrases[i] is a valid phrase: 1 <= len(p) <= 100; every byte p[t] with 0 <= t < len(p) is either 32 (space) or a lowercase ASCII letter with code 97..122; p[0] != 32; p[len(p)-1] != 32; and for every t with 0 <= t < len(p)-1, not (p[t] = 32 and p[t+1] = 32). Words in a phrase are its maximal non-space substrings; the first word is the prefix before the first space, or the whole phrase if there is no space; the last word is the suffix after the last space, or the whole phrase if there is no space.
